instruction.what: The evidence validation (B5) of one subgroup, after its sweep, the gate before 3.1: the code checks of its observations (shown in `code_checks`), and the reading of every evidence observation of the subgroup (its own of S1 to 2.1, and the older ones on its occurrences kept as evidence) for whether it is true, founded and coherent with the others. Inner being is not judged here; the two validations are never run together.
read: Read the code checks first: a failing check names observations to repair (unmarked, no node, a word node missing a column without its reason, a trace to a deleted observation, two of one text, a B1 observation no sense traces, a sense the 2.1 observations on its occurrences do not trace, an older observation left open).

Take one observation at a time (`observations`, in the order of the steps): its text, basis and grounds against its verses (`verses`) and the observations it traces. Is it true of those verses? Does it say more than they show? Does it contradict another observation of the subgroup?
write: Fill `answer.observations`, one entry for each observation of the package: verdict true, with `why` (what in the verses and the data bears it out); or verdict repair, with `why` (what is wrong) and `actions`: the actions of the validation that repair it (cfg_setting validate.reading actions, each with its parameters, for example {"action": "restate", "oid": id, "new_text": ..., "checked": ..., "reason": ...}, or delete_neither, complete_node, add_trace).
A repair is checked as it is written; an observation that cannot be made true is deleted with its reason.

Then: Collection-Build.ps1 -Action RecordEvidence -File <the answer file> (-Check to preview), and ReadEvidence again until every evidence observation is read; the gate passes when all are read and the code checks pass.

keep.text: A sheet of validation actions is checked whole (every action named, its parameters complete) and written in one transaction: any action the tables refuse refuses the whole sheet and nothing is kept. -Check runs every action and rolls back. Every change is kept in ib_observation_change with its reason (RW-01); nothing is physically deleted.

A finding of the validation is repaired first: a wording that is untrue or stronger than its verse is restated and the restatement checked against the base data; a node missing a column is completed, or the reason the data cannot give it is recorded; a duplicate is consolidated; a node is deleted only when another live node carries its occurrence or it supports no finding of its observation. A finding is left open only when a named collection's validation will touch the observation: the deferral to that collection and the finding are recorded, and the check accepts it as deferred. A finding with no named owner is closed in the validation.

An older observation is deleted as consumed only when live observations carry its meaning: every word occurrence of it is on a live node of a carrier or named as not carried with its reason, the mapping is stated in words (what the old says, which carrier states each part), the traces to it are re-pointed or replaced, and the consumption is kept as `consumed_by`. An observation that holds more than one finding is split first.

An observation that is neither evidence nor inner being contributes nothing to the purposes of the observations (researcher, 2026-11-22): it is commented with its reason and the word occurrences no other live observation holds, then deleted. An observation already marked, or one another observation traces, is not deleted this way.

Evidence states what the data are or show, tied to a verse. Inner being states how something works in the inner being, based on evidence, a building block of the stage 5 claims. The marker (ib_observation.nature) follows the content and purpose of the observation, never its stage (RS-04): an observation of any stage may be inner being when it traces to evidence. One that states both is split. The marker is set when the observation is created, by the item that is answered (cfg_setting layer.reading items.<item>.nature); a finding file never sets it; the validation changes it only where the content shows the item's nature does not hold.

The validation runs in two layers, never concurrently: evidence first, then inner being. The inner-being layer is judged only when the evidence layer passes (every in-scope observation marked, none without a live node, no word node missing a required column without its reason, no live trace to a deleted observation, no two of one meaning). A later evidence change reopens only the inner-being rows it touches. In the build this gate is: step 3.1 does not open before the evidence layer passes, and step 3.3 does not close before both layers pass (cfg_setting layer.reading open_gate and closing_gate).
No observation is changed except by a reading, and every change is recorded with its reason. An observation no longer supported by the verse is soft-deleted, with the reason.
One observation per finding: the same description is never written twice. Applied to another verse, word or scope it gains a node on the existing observation.
Observation text is concise and tied to this verse's content, never a restatement of the word's dictionary sense. A transliteration is never given without its gloss.
Verse references are resolved fresh at write time, never taken from the text written. Relations are recorded only on evidence.
Missing data in the base extract is named as a gap, never substituted from memory or outside knowledge.

observations.text: In Exo 2:14, Rut 4:4, 1Sa 20:3, 2Ki 7:12, Act 12:9, Rom 1:21, Rom 14:14, Ecc 9:10 and 2Cor 10:5 knowing stands beside a person's own thought: Moses fears the deed is known, Saul keeps Jonathan from knowing, Peter did not know the vision was real, those who knew God became futile in thinking, and every thought is brought under the knowledge of God. In Mat 22:16 and Mar 12:14 the questioners claim to know Jesus is true.
observations.grounds: although they knew God, they did not honor him

observations.text: In Psa 92:5 and Isa 66:18 the Lord's works and thoughts, and people's works and thoughts known to him, are named together: the thoughts stand with the deeds. In Neh 6:9 the enemies think the hands will drop from the work, in Ecc 9:10 there is no work or thought in Sheol, in Mat 21:28 work is the son's task in the case asked about, and in Eph 3:20 God's power at work goes beyond what we think.
observations.grounds: I know their works and their thoughts

observations.text: In 1Sa 20:3 Saul thinks to keep the matter from Jonathan lest he be grieved: the thought is to spare his son grief.
observations.grounds: lest he be grieved

observations.text: In Mar 6:49 the disciples think they see a ghost and cry out: the cry follows the mistaken thought. In Deu 15:9 the poor brother may cry to the Lord against the one whose unworthy thought made him grudging.
observations.grounds: they thought it was a ghost, and cried out

observations.text: Life and death are what the thought concerns in 1Sa 20:3 (David's oath on the Lord who lives), 1Sa 27:11 and 2Ki 7:12 (none left alive, taking them alive), and Act 26:8 (God raising the dead thought incredible). In Dan 5:10 the queen wishes the king life as his thoughts alarm him, in Luk 13:4 the dead are compared with all who lived in Jerusalem, in Dan 2:30 Daniel claims no wisdom above all the living, and in Heb 4:12 the living word discerns the thoughts.
observations.grounds: the word of God is living and active

observations.text: In Deu 15:9 the unworthy thought in the heart is that the year of release is near, so the poor brother is refused: the thought turns the release into a reason to withhold. In Jer 40:4 Jeremiah is released from chains and told to go where he thinks good.
observations.grounds: the year of release is near

observations.text: In Psa 139:17 God's thoughts are precious to the psalmist: the thoughts are loved. In Judg 15:2 the father thought Samson hated his daughter: a mistaken thought about love. In Dan 4:19 Daniel's alarming thoughts concern the dream he wishes on those who hate the king, and in 2Cor 12:19 Paul answers what the beloved have been thinking.
observations.grounds: How precious to me are your thoughts, O God

observations.text: In Exo 2:14, Judg 3:24, 1Sa 16:6, 1Sa 20:26 and 2Ki 5:11 surely marks the certainty of the quoted thought, and each time the thought is wrong or overturned: the deed is known, the king is relieving himself, the anointed is before him, he is unclean, the prophet will come out. In Psa 48:9 and Psa 94:18 the thought is set on the Lord's steadfast love, which holds up the one whose foot slips; in 2Ch 32:1 the acts of faithfulness come before Sennacherib's plan, and in Heb 11:11 the one counted faithful is God.
observations.grounds: your steadfast love, O Lord, held me up

observations.text: In Isa 66:18 the Lord who knows their works and thoughts will gather the nations to see his glory: the knowing of thoughts precedes the showing of glory.
observations.grounds: they shall come and shall see my glory

observations.text: In Luk 1:51 the Lord acts with his strong arm against those proud in their inner reasonings: his might is set against proud thoughts. In Ecc 9:10 the hand is to work with might, for there is no thought in Sheol.
observations.grounds: he has scattered the proud in the thoughts of their hearts

observations.text: In Psa 50:21 the Lord was silent and the people thought him like themselves: his silence was taken for sameness. In 2Sa 14:17 the woman thought the king's word would set her at rest. In 1Cor 7:40 Paul thinks she is happier if she remains, and in 1Pe 4:1 the way of thinking to arm oneself with goes with having ceased from sin.
observations.grounds: These things you have done, and I have been silent

observations.text: In Gen 32:20 Jacob thinks to appease Esau with the present sent ahead: the gift is the means the thought plans. In Rut 4:4 Boaz thought to put the offer before the elders, in Jer 40:5 Jeremiah is given a present and told to go where he thinks right, and in 1Cor 7:26 Paul judges in view of the present distress.
observations.grounds: I may appease him with the present that goes ahead of me

observations.text: In Num 5:28 the woman found clean shall be free and conceive children: conceive is bodily, and free names her release from the curse; no thought is in view.
observations.grounds: she shall be free and shall conceive children

observations.text: In 2Ki 7:12 the king thinks the Syrians know the people are hungry and lie in wait: the hunger is the ground of the enemy's supposed plan. In Luk 13:2 the hearers are asked whether they think those who suffered were worse sinners, and in 1Pe 4:1 Christ's suffering in the flesh is the way of thinking to arm oneself with.
observations.grounds: Do you think that these Galileans were worse sinners

observations.text: In Eze 38:10 thoughts come into Gog's mind and he devises an evil scheme: the thoughts arise first and the scheme follows from them.
observations.grounds: you will devise an evil scheme

observations.text: In Job 32:6, Job 32:10 and Job 32:17 Elihu holds back and then declares his opinion: the view is spoken out. In Psa 40:5 the psalmist would proclaim the Lord's thoughts, in Isa 55:8 the Lord declares his thoughts are not theirs, and in Amo 4:13 he declares to man what is his thought. In Dan 5:10 the queen speaks to the king whose thoughts alarm him, and in Phili 1:17 some proclaim Christ thinking to afflict Paul.
observations.grounds: declares to man what is his thought

observations.text: In Lam 1:9 Jerusalem took no thought of her future, and the enemy has triumphed: the lack of thought ends in the enemy's victory.
observations.grounds: she took no thought of her future

observations.text: Pride and the thoughts go together in Psa 10:4 (in the pride of his face the wicked's thoughts deny God), Luk 1:51 (the proud are scattered in their inner reasonings) and 2Cor 10:5 (every lofty opinion against the knowledge of God is pulled down and the thoughts taken captive). In Jam 1:26 the one who thinks himself religious has a worthless religion.
observations.grounds: In the pride of his face the wicked does not seek him

observations.text: The thought is given in an answer or reply in Gen 31:31, Exo 2:14, Est 4:13, Job 32:6, Job 32:17, Dan 4:19, Luk 5:22 and Luk 13:2: a person explains or corrects a thought in speech. In Job 20:2 the thoughts themselves answer Zophar.
observations.grounds: my thoughts answer me

observations.text: In 2Cor 9:5 Paul thought it needful that the promised gift be ready: the judgment serves the promise. In Num 11:12 and Heb 11:11 promise and swearing stand with conceive in its bodily sense: Moses did not conceive the people the Lord swore to, and Sarah counted faithful the one who promised.
observations.grounds: the gift you have promised

observations.text: In 2Ki 20:19 and Isa 39:8 Hezekiah thinks there will be peace in his days: the thought rests on his own peace. In Mat 10:34 and Luk 12:51 the hearers are not to think Jesus came to bring peace: the false thought is corrected by a sword and division.
observations.grounds: Do not think that I have come to bring peace

observations.text: In Job 12:5 the thought of one at ease is ready with contempt for those whose feet slip. In 2Cor 9:5 Paul judged it needful that the gift be ready as a willing gift.
observations.grounds: it is ready for those whose feet slip

observations.text: In Act 12:9 Peter did not know what the angel did was real and thought it a vision: the thought takes the real for unreal. In Phili 4:8 whatever is true is what to think on. In Mat 22:16 and Mar 12:14 the questioners call Jesus true, not swayed by anyone's standing.
observations.grounds: He did not know that what was being done by the angel was real

observations.text: In 2Ki 18:20 and Isa 36:5 the Rabshakeh asks whether they think mere words are strength for war, and in whom they trust that they have rebelled: the question mocks the thought on which their rebellion rests.
observations.grounds: In whom do you now trust, that you have rebelled against me

observations.text: In Psa 119:52 the psalmist thinks of the Lord's rules from of old: the thought reaches back to what is ancient. In 2Sa 21:16 the giant with his fresh weapon meant to strike David down.
observations.grounds: your rules from of old

observations.text: In Gen 32:20 Jacob thinks Esau may accept him after the present: the thought hopes for acceptance. In 2Cor 11:16 Paul asks that no one think him foolish, but if they do, to accept him as a fool.
observations.grounds: perhaps he will accept me

observations.text: In 1Ch 29:18 David prays that the Lord hold his people's willing purposes in their hearts for ever: the thoughts are to be kept by God. In Dan 7:28 Daniel's thoughts alarm him and he keeps the matter in his heart.
observations.grounds: I kept the matter in my heart

observations.text: In Isa 55:7 the unrighteous man is to forsake his thoughts and return to the Lord: return follows the forsaking. In Jer 3:7 the Lord thought Israel would return, but she did not. In Heb 11:15 had they been thinking of the land they left they could have returned: the thinking would have led back. In Jer 40:5 Jeremiah may return to Gedaliah or go where he thinks right.
observations.grounds: but she did not return

observations.text: In Eze 20:32 the thought in the people's mind is to be like the nations and worship wood and stone: the thought is of idolatry, and the Lord says it shall never be.
observations.grounds: worship wood and stone

observations.text: In Deu 15:9 the thought in the heart is unworthy, and it leads to withholding from the poor. In Heb 10:29 the hearers are asked to think how much worse the punishment is for the one who profaned the covenant. In Mat 22:17 and Mar 12:14 paying taxes is the matter Jesus is asked his view of.
observations.grounds: an unworthy thought in your heart

observations.text: In Psa 40:17 the Lord takes thought for the poor and needy speaker: the Lord's thought is turned to the poor. In Deu 15:9 the unworthy thought turns the eye grudgingly from the poor brother, and in Joh 13:29 some think Judas was sent to give to the poor. In Ecc 10:20 even in thought one is not to curse the rich. In Isa 55:7 and Eph 3:20 abundantly names God's pardon and power beyond what is thought; in Mic 2:8 the rich robe is stripped from those with no thought of war.
observations.grounds: the Lord takes thought for me

observations.text: In Pro 12:5 the thoughts of the righteous are just, set against the counsels of the wicked; in Phili 4:8 what is just and honorable is what to think on. In Job 35:2 Elihu asks whether Job thinks his claim just. In Mat 15:19 and Mar 7:21 sexual immorality follows evil thoughts out of the heart. In Isa 59:4 no one sues justly where mischief is conceived, in 2Cor 12:6 Paul speaks the truth so none may think more of him, and in Mat 22:17 and Mar 12:14 what is lawful is the question put to Jesus.
observations.grounds: The thoughts of the righteous are just

observations.text: In Psa 40:17 the Lord who takes thought for the poor is his help and deliverer. In Jer 4:14 Jerusalem is to wash her heart to be saved, while wicked thoughts lodge within: the thoughts stand in the way of saving. In Rut 4:4 Boaz thought to tell the kinsman of the right to redeem, and in Judg 13:5 the son conceived will begin to save Israel.
observations.grounds: wash your heart from evil, that you may be saved

observations.text: In Job 12:5 the thought of one at ease holds contempt for misfortune: contempt is in the thought. In Mat 15:19 slander is among what comes out of the heart with evil thoughts.
observations.grounds: there is contempt for misfortune

observations.text: In 1Ch 28:9 and Psa 139:23 the Lord searches the heart and knows the thoughts: searching is the way the thoughts are known. In Psa 10:4 the wicked does not seek God, and his thoughts deny him. In 2Sa 10:3 and 1Ch 19:3 the princes think David's servants came to search out the city, and in Joh 5:39 the hearers search the Scriptures because they think life is in them. In Mat 18:12 and Ecc 9:10 search and find stand in the case asked about and in the call to work while there is thought.
observations.grounds: Search me, O God, and know my heart

observations.text: In Rom 12:3 one is to think of oneself with sober judgment, not more highly than one ought: the thinking is to be measured. In 2Cor 12:6 Paul refrains from boasting so that no one thinks more of him than is due.
observations.grounds: to think with sober judgment

observations.text: In Num 33:56 the Lord will do to Israel as he thought to do to the nations: the thought is carried into deed. In Luk 12:17 the rich man thinks what to do with his crops, in 1Cor 7:36 the one who thinks he behaves badly toward his betrothed may do as he wishes, and in Ecc 9:10 the hand is to do with might while there is thought. In 1Ch 28:9 Solomon is to serve God with a willing mind, in Joh 16:2 the killer thinks he serves God, and in Phili 2:25 Paul thought it needful to send Epaphroditus his minister. In Eph 3:20 God does more than we think, and in Mar 12:14 the questioners speak of Jesus' way.
observations.grounds: I will do to you as I thought to do to them

observations.text: Giving follows the thought in Judg 15:2 (the father gave his daughter away because he thought Samson hated her), 1Sa 18:17 and 1Sa 18:21 (Saul gives his daughter thinking to snare David), and Jer 3:19 (the Lord thought to give a pleasant land). In Deu 15:9 the unworthy thought keeps one from giving to the poor, and in Joh 13:29 some think Judas was to give to the poor. In Luk 8:18, Luk 12:51, Rom 12:3, Jer 40:5, Dan 7:25 and Job 32:17 giving names grace given, peace not given, a gift, the saints given over, and Elihu's share; in Job 15:35 and Isa 7:14 birth and sign go with conceive, and in 1Cor 13:11 childish thinking is given up.
observations.grounds: I really thought that you utterly hated her, so I gave her

observations.text: In Isa 59:7 the thoughts are thoughts of iniquity, and in Isa 59:4 mischief is conceived and iniquity born: sin is the content of the thoughts. In Deu 15:9 the unworthy thought that withholds from the poor becomes sin. In Luk 13:2 the hearers are asked whether they think the Galileans were worse sinners, in 1Cor 7:36 the one who thinks he behaves badly does not sin by marrying, and in 1Pe 4:1 the way of thinking armed with goes with ceasing from sin. In Psa 51:5 sin is the state in which the psalmist was conceived.
observations.grounds: their thoughts are thoughts of iniquity

observations.text: In Eph 3:20 God is able to do more than we ask or think: his power exceeds the reach of thought.
observations.grounds: far more abundantly than all that we ask or think
